s.note: Cheddar and roasted capsicum spread with crackers
s.how: Finely grate 200g vintage cheddar. Mix with 100g mayonnaise, 80g chopped roasted red capsicum from a jar, 1 tsp Worcestershire, a pinch of cayenne and black pepper until combined but still chunky. Chill 30 minutes. Spoon into a bowl, dust with paprika and serve with 200g crackers, celery sticks and a few cornichons.

s.note: Cornmeal crumbed green tomatoes fried crisp, with a buttermilk herb dressing
s.how: Salt the tomato slices and leave 10 minutes, then pat dry. Dip each slice in 150ml of the buttermilk, then in the polenta, flour and paprika mixed. Fry in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes a side until golden. Drain. Whisk the rest of the buttermilk with the mayonnaise, chopped chives and a squeeze of lemon. Serve the tomatoes hot with the dressing.

m.n: Park picnic ham and spinach frittata
m.note: Baked frittata with ham, potato, spinach and feta
m.how: Boil 300g diced potato for 8 minutes and drain. Fry 1 sliced onion in 1 tbsp oil in a 26cm ovenproof pan for 5 minutes, add the potato, 150g diced ham and 100g baby spinach and stir until wilted. Whisk 8 eggs with 100ml cream and salt, pour over and scatter with 100g crumbled feta. Cook on low for 5 minutes, then bake at 180C for 15 minutes until set. Serve with rocket dressed in lemon and relish.

m.note: Bradley frees Sandy from the vending machine.
m.how: Soak the chicken in the buttermilk with the hot sauce and a pinch of salt for at least 1 hour. Whisk the self-raising flour, eggs, milk and melted butter into a smooth batter. Cook the waffles in a hot greased waffle iron until crisp and keep warm in a low oven. Dredge the chicken in the plain flour mixed with the paprika, salt and pepper, and fry at 170°C for 5 to 6 minutes until golden and cooked through. Warm the maple syrup with a dash of hot sauce. Stack the chicken on the waffles, pour over the maple and serve with the spinach dressed in lemon juice and a little oil.

w.note: Scones with balsamic strawberries and cream
w.how: Slice 300g strawberries and toss with 1 tbsp caster sugar and 1 tsp balsamic vinegar and leave 20 minutes. Rub 80g cold butter into 250g self-raising flour and 2 tbsp sugar, add 150ml milk and pat out to 2cm. Cut 6 rounds, brush with milk and bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Whip 300ml cream with 1 tbsp icing sugar and 1 tsp vanilla. Split the shortcakes and fill with cream and strawberries.

w.note: Almond croissants, Russell's mum on Skype.
w.how: Simmer 100g caster sugar with 100ml water and 1 tsp vanilla for 2 minutes. Beat 80g soft butter, 80g caster sugar, 1 egg and 100g almond meal into a paste. Split 4 croissants, brush the insides with syrup and spread with half the almond cream. Close, spread the rest on top and scatter with 30g flaked almonds. Bake at 180C for 15 minutes. Dust with icing sugar and serve with jam.

d.note: Blood orange juice, orange liqueur and sparkling wine
d.how: Juice 6 blood oranges or regular oranges and strain. Pour 60ml juice and 10ml orange liqueur into each of 4 flutes. Slowly top with chilled sparkling wine, about 100ml per glass. Garnish with a thin orange wheel on the rim. For the kids, mix the rest of the juice with soda water.
